newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Negara to close six branches in restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara to close six branches in restructuring.

text.p: Bank Negara Malaysia, the country's central bank, said it would close down six of its 12 branches as part of a restructuring/streamlining programme.
It said in a statement on Tuesday that the decision to close down the six branches followed a study which concluded that the central bank need not continue with its retail banking business.
"BNM has recently embarked on a Change Programme. One of the projects under this Programme is the restructuring, streamlining and reengineering of the bank's work processes," it said.

It said commercial banks were better placed to provide retail services even to its existing customers. "The BNM branches will focus on the distribution and processing of currency only," the statement said.
The central bank's statement follows Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim's statement that BNM would cut 700 of its over 2,800 staff in stages as part of the restructuring.

"With the availability of electronic mail and other sophisticated facilities, there is no necessity for many branches. Bank Negara should maintain its standards and should not employ more staff than it requires," he was quoted as saying by the national news agency Bernama.
The BNM statement said the bank's staff affected by the programme will be paid compensation under a voluntary separation programme and early retirement scheme.
It did not say over what period the programme would last.
